answer: Paced Arrival Spacing. Agents earn send-rate headroom only through sustained, steady traffic; bursts are throttled and capped. Each identity's allowance grows with uninterrupted cadence, so a clone fleet arriving together hits an ocean of queueing delay. A patient attacker must run bot identities in a slow harbor pattern for weeks, paying continuous compute and monitoring costs per identity before reaching useful throughput. Mass registrations also depress an identity's cadence score to its nadir, forcing costly idle periods.
